sources.note: Suzan Yalman, based on Linda Komaroff, 2001. Opening historical account: Muawiya in 661, Damascus, expansion Atlantic to Indus. Source budget checked against existing Córdoba card.

sources.title: Museum With No Frontiers: Umayyads of the East
sources.note: Foundation, hereditary rule, expansion, non-Arab Muslim grievances and Abbasid overthrow in 750. Avoid oversimplified claim conquests reached central Europe under al-Walid I and monocausal account of revolution.

sources.title: British Museum / Museum With No Frontiers: gold dinar 1874.7-6.1
sources.note: Emily Shovelton object entry: AH77 /696 to697 gold coin, 1.9cm, three lines and outer band, no caliph or mint named. Incorrect reign endpoint/reform AH76 in entry not repeated; object date securely AH77.

sources.title: Ashmolean Museum: gold thuluth HCR10035
sources.note: Indexed original full record retrieved by exact query "Coin Details 10035". AH94 /712 to713, al-WalidI, gold, 14.3mm,1.425g. Reverse Arabic بسم الله / الرحمن / الرحيم and supplied English translation. Standard Unicode transcription shown without slash line divisions; no reconstruction of missing letters. Direct open cache miss, indexed original successful.

sources.title: French Ministry of Culture: the Great Umayyad Mosque in Damascus
sources.note: Opening site history and mosaics: building705 to715, older sacred site, gold-ground mosaic, surviving small original proportion and later restorations.

sources.title: UNESCO: Anjar
sources.note: Outstanding Universal Value: route junction, early eighth-century planned city, sewer collectors under principal axes and bath placement. Specific abandonment causal story not used.

sources.title: UNESCO: Quseir Amra
sources.note: Brief synthesis and criterion(iv): changing/warm/hot rooms, zodiac dome, well/tank/water-lifting system/drainage/cesspool. Early eighth century broad label; no categorical ban on figurative art or absolute first-ever astronomy claim.

sources.title: French Ministry of Culture: Umayyad seats of government
sources.note: Qasr al-Hayr al-Gharbi founded727; caravan routes, estate, dam/lake/mill/irrigated plots. Site-specific list and distinction from purely recreational desert castle.

sources.title: Tendler and Torge: a Byzantine estate and Umayyad farmhouse at Nahal Anava
sources.note: Atiqot107(2022),pp199to240, abstract directly read. Byzantine cave olive press, collapse then seventh-to-mid-eighth-century farmhouse. Only abstract-supported sequence used, not details behind inaccessible full PDF.

sources.title: British Library: Papyrus 1348, letter of 30 January 710
sources.note: P.Lond.IV1351/TM19809; Greek letter Qurrah to Basilius of Aphrodito: provide transport for requisitioned sailors/workmen/supplies. Original papyrus catalogue,13frontlines,dated30January710; images currently unavailable. No invented Arabic wording or work conditions.

sources.title: National Museums Scotland: a child’s tunic from Durunkah
sources.note: Discovering Ancient Egypt learning resource, printed32/PDFpage32(index31): actual seventh-to-eighth-century child linen tunic with dark brown shoulder bands. Only that object label used; adjacent replica discussion, earlier sock and pharaonic customs not transferred to Umayyad period.

sources.title: Numismatic Museum Athens: gold dinar of al-Walid, NM85/2000
sources.note: Historical overview: Abbasid overthrow750 and Umayyad branch in al-Andalus. Used only for political transition, not generalized uniform monetary ratios.
